subject: Nmix & site-occ models, and JAGS, in production mode

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: Nmix & site-occ models, and JAGS, in production mode
parts:
Dear all,

 

we are proud to present the new Swiss breeding bird atlas:  Knaus, P., Antoniazza, S., Wechsler, S., Guélat, J., Kéry, M., Strebel, N. & Sattler, T. 2018. Brutvogelatlas 2013–2016. Bestandsentwicklung der Brutvögel der Schweiz und des Fürstentums Liechtensteins (Swiss Breeding Bird Atlas 2013–2016). Schweizerische Vogelwarte, Sempach.  See also here: https://www.vogelwarte.ch/en/projects/monitoring/swiss-breeding-bird-atlas. You can buy your copy in German or in French (the Italian version is sold out) and you can send me an email if you're interested in receiving a free pdf in any of these languages.

 

In addition, here you can download the English pdf of the entire atlas for free: https://www.dropbox.com/s/46s6x2tg16be3k1/SwissBreedingBirdAtlas_2013_2016.pdf?dl=0.

 

We think that this atlas sets new standards in several methodological ways:

--- It must be one of the first breeding bird atlases, worldwide, that attempts to produce the species abundance and distribution maps with accommodation of both imperfect detection and spatial autocorrelation (in addition to a bunch of environmental covariates) for as many species as possible (132).

--- That is, this atlas represents probably one of the biggest practical applications of the binomial N-mixture model (Royle, Biometrics, 2004) and of the site-occupancy model (MacKenzie et al., Ecology, 2002; Tyre et al., Ecol. App., 2003). In addition, a spatial (search-encounter) capture recapture model (Royle et al., MEE, 2011) was used for estimation of national population sizes for several dozens of the more common species.

--- And finally, this atlas demonstrates that BUGS software can be used to fit such models at a fairly large spatial scale: we used JAGS to fit all the Nmix and site-occ models, with splines for spatial autocorrelation, to the 42,000 1 km2 squares in Switzerland.

 

We hope that this atlas can serve as an encouragement for more widespread incorporation of a rigorous specification of the observation error in statistical analyses in biodiversity monitoring projects and in species distribution models (SDMs). We think that our atlas demonstrates that these models, which can be implemented in BUGS software, have definitely left the R&D phase and have moved on to the 'production phase.'

 

Best regards  ----  Marc
